clue.text: Put up in church but it may be loose

indicators.note: in tells us the word for put up goes inside the word for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to put up a picture is to hang it

explanation.surface: Something hung in a church that might come loose, like a notice or a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins in a pocket are called loose change, so this is a thing that may be loose.

clue.text: Infection around spot needs cream applied regularly

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for around
a spot can be a hole, as in a tight spot

indicators.note: applied regularly picks out every other letter of the word cream

explanation.surface: An infected spot needs a cream rubbed on regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is a bacterial infection of the gut spread by dirty water.

clue.text: A mountain that's good to climb

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: to climb in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: ah is an exclamation of satisfaction

explanation.surface: Praise for a mountain worth climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like the article but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet and the radio code word for the letter.

clue.text: Say, John Brown lying in his grave starts to rise! It's not true

indicators.note: to rise in a down clue means those letters are read upwards
starts picks out the first letter of each of the four words

parts.note: a lie is something untrue

explanation.surface: A nod to the song where John Brown's body lies in the grave, then a claim that he rises.
explanation.walkthrough: John Brown was Queen Victoria's Scottish servant and ghillie; the song 'John Brown's Body' is the other John Brown.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghillie is a Scottish hunting or fishing attendant; John Brown served Queen Victoria as one.

clue.text: Talk in backroom of pub was effective

parts.note: read as back room of pub: a bar is a room in a pub, and back turns it round
brakes that bit were effective; bite means take hold

explanation.surface: Chatting in the back room of a pub did the trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backroom' looks like one word but splits: 'back' turns BAR into RAB. 'Talk' as a verb is British slang: to rabbit (on) is to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit, or rabbit on, is to chatter at length.

clue.text: Lost drunk butts in here

indicators.note: drunk tells us the word is spoken with a slur, so an extra sound creeps in

parts.note: something lost has gone astray

explanation.surface: A lost drunk barges in.
explanation.walkthrough: A slurring drunk says S as SH. 'butts in' looks like interrupting but means cigarette ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Cigarette ends, or butts, are stubbed out and left in this dish.

clue.text: Supports politician — it's happened before now

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician recalls past support.
explanation.definitionFit: A backstory is the history behind a character or situation: events that happened earlier.

clue.text: Lady sat round wrapping present

indicators.note: wrapping tells us the rearranged letters go around the word for present
round suggests the letters turn about and are rearranged

parts.note: present, as in at hand, means here

explanation.surface: A woman sits wrapping a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but means in attendance; the anagram signalled by 'round' gives TSA, which does the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so an example of a lady.

clue.text: Keeps stopping a performance car — stunned

indicators.note: stopping, as in plugging a gap, means one word goes inside the others

parts.note: GT stands for gran turismo, a high-performance car
to keep something is to have it

explanation.surface: Someone keeps stalling a sports car, leaving onlookers amazed.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means struck with horror or amazement, so stunned is a close synonym.

clue.text: Getting on to police — pinching conkers!

indicators.note: police as a verb means control or keep in order, so these letters are rearranged into order

explanation.surface: An old grump heads to the police station to report children stealing conkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'police' looks like a noun but is a verb, working on PINCHING CONKERS. Conkers are horse-chestnut seeds British children play a game with.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone said to be no spring chicken is no longer young, i.e. getting on in years.

clue.text: Sell right Yorkshire bitter, I'd say

indicators.note: I'd say tells us the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect right is reet and the ale is t'ale, so this is spoken as reet t'ale

explanation.surface: A Yorkshireman recommends a genuine local bitter to sell.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speech says 'reet' for right and shortens 'the' to t', so 'reet t'ale' is heard. Bitter is a British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To retail goods is to sell them to the public, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Stopped one looking embarrassed about lie

parts.note: one is A, as in a single item

indicators.note: about tells us the colour goes round the word for lie

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red
to lie down is to rest

explanation.surface: Someone caught out blushes over a lie they told.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrested means halted or checked, as in arrested development: stopped in its progress.

clue.text: State cover up these outrageous criminal charges

indicators.note: State as a verb means say out loud, so the next word is to be heard

parts.note: to wrap something is to cover it up

indicators.note: outrageous suggests something wild, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A government cover-up of something scandalous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a government noun but is the verb 'say', and WRAP said aloud gives RAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap sheet is an American term for a person's record of arrests and criminal charges.

clue.text: Comforted, having been duped by The Voice

indicators.note: by the voice tells us the word is heard spoken, not read

parts.note: to be suckered is to be duped

explanation.surface: Someone consoled after being fooled by the TV talent show The Voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Voice' looks like the TV show but just means spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To succour someone is to help and console them in distress.

clue.text: Performed valiantly in the old country

parts.note: ye is an old spelling of the
Oman is a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: Someone fought bravely back in the old country.
explanation.walkthrough: Used as an adjective, as in 'yeoman service', the word describes work done loyally and valiantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeoman service is loyal, valiant help, so the word can describe something performed valiantly.

clue.text: Charm shown by Nicola Sturgeon, perhaps, to a degree

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
Nicola Sturgeon, then First Minister of Scotland, is an example of a Scot

explanation.surface: Nicola Sturgeon displaying charm, up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a lucky charm, an object thought to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Rings low down financial advisers after head vanishes (we should, too)

indicators.note: after head vanishes means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a bank advises customers on money
let's means let us, i.e. we should

explanation.surface: Low-down advisers vanish with the money, and we should too.
explanation.definitionFit: Anklets are ornamental bands worn round the ankle, so rings worn low down.

clue.text: Guides through dark hills, guerilla-infested

indicators.note: infested means the guerrilla is put inside the hills

parts.note: tors are rocky hills, as on Dartmoor
Che Guevara was a famous guerrilla

explanation.surface: Guides lead the way through hills crawling with guerrillas.
explanation.definitionFit: Torches are lights carried to show the way through darkness.

clue.text: Criticising what solvers are doing? No point

indicators.note: No tells us the abbreviation for point is left out

parts.note: solvers of codes are decrypting

explanation.surface: A setter complains that solvers are wasting their time.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrying something is running it down, i.e. criticising it publicly.

clue.text: Cancel date set up online

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a television set is a tele
E is short for electronic, as in email

explanation.surface: Calling off a date arranged on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete is to strike out or erase, so to cancel.

clue.text: Focus here on nothing, right? Complain!

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the rest

parts.note: to carp is to complain
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a fuss over nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Focus' is the Ford Focus car, and the question mark says it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A carport is a shelter for cars, so a Ford Focus could be parked there.

clue.text: Maureen left for Spain after bust-up, as I was in Rome

indicators.note: a bust-up is a fight, so the letters break up and are rearranged
for means one letter replaces another

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Maureen leaves Spain after a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts L in place of an E in MAUREEN, making MAURLEN, which 'bust-up' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: I is the Roman figure for one, so in Rome it served as a number symbol.

clue.text: Old barrister: "Men have spoken about scene of fatal shootings"

indicators.note: about tells us the word for spoken goes round the other pieces

parts.note: oral means spoken
KC is King's Counsel, a senior barrister; with a Queen on the throne in 2015 the title was an old one
OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A retired lawyer quotes a statement given by some men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old barrister' is KC (King's Counsel), the title used under a king, and 'Men' are OR, other ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1881 Gunfight at the OK Corral in Tombstone, Arizona, left three men dead.

clue.text: Men are set to put a new handle on

definitions.text: to put a new handle on

indicators.note: set as in arranged or put in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Men are ready to fit a new handle to a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' looks like a door handle but is slang for a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Handle is slang for a name, so giving something a new one is to call it something else.

clue.text: Japanese-American in thirties interviewed for promotion

indicators.note: for promotion says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Japanese-American in their thirties interviewed for a better job.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'for promotion' means upwards; 'in' marks the letters hidden in 'thirties interviewed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nisei are the US-born children of Japanese immigrants, a second-generation group.

clue.text: To be the boss's squeeze was sheer torture

indicators.note: to squeeze is to crush and distort, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that their boss's girlfriend made life miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeeze' looks like a noun meaning a lover, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: whoever wears the trousers in a household is the one in charge.

clue.text: Grey, maybe, or blue? It's tricky

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters need sorting, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is a colour grey or blue? Hard to tell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grey' looks like a colour beside 'blue', but is Christian Grey, the cruel lover of Fifty Shades of Grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian Grey of Fifty Shades of Grey enjoys inflicting pain, an example of a cruel person.

clue.text: A weave whenever you fancy it

parts.note: twill is a weave with diagonal ridges

explanation.surface: A cloth woven whenever the weaver likes.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something as you will means doing it whenever you choose, as you please.
